lines: Don't leave me in the Basalt Deltas. The ground looks sharp enough to cut through courage.
The Basalt Deltas are ash, basalt, and misery. I needed you back a lot sooner.
I stood in the Basalt Deltas trying not to think about lava finding a path to my feet.
If you must wander off, do not do it in the Basalt Deltas where everything feels broken and hot.
Every crack in the ground looked like it wanted to become a problem.
The ash made it hard to see, and the heat made it hard to think.
Please do not leave me somewhere the floor feels angry.
The Basalt Deltas made every step sound like stone breaking under a bad decision.
I kept watching for lava, loose rock, and anything else that wanted me gone.
I was alone in a place made of heat, ash, and sharp edges, hoping you remembered the way back.
Don't leave me in the Crimson Forest. Everything there looks alive in the worst possible way.
The Crimson Forest is red, loud, and unsettling enough with company. Alone is worse.
I was stuck in the Crimson Forest watching every fungus patch like it might <jump>lunge</jump>.
If you wander off in the Crimson Forest, do not expect me to enjoy waiting for you.
The whole place felt like it was breathing around me.
I kept hearing movement and could not tell if it was the forest or something in it.
Please do not leave me somewhere the walls look like flesh and the trees look hungry.
The Crimson Forest made every shadow feel warm, close, and wrong.
I was trying not to stare too long at anything, because everything looked ready to stare back.
Being alone there felt less like waiting and more like being noticed.
Don't leave me in the Nether Wastes. Heat, ash, and open lava are not fair company.
The Nether Wastes are exactly where I never want to be abandoned.
I waited in the Nether Wastes trying not to look at every lava pool like it was leaning closer.
If you disappear in the Nether Wastes, I am left in the middle of fire and bad choices.
There is nowhere there that feels like shelter, only places that are slightly less on fire.
The heat made every breath feel borrowed.
Please do not leave me somewhere even the air feels hostile.
The Nether Wastes made the whole world feel like a furnace with no door.
I kept watching the lava, the ledges, and the sky, and none of them made me feel better.
I was alone in a burning wasteland, hoping you came back before something worse did.
Don't leave me in the Soul Sand Valley. Even the ground there fights every step.
The Soul Sand Valley is bad enough when I can move quickly. Alone, I cannot.
I waited in the Soul Sand Valley trying not to panic while the ground slowed me down.
If you vanish in a Soul Sand Valley, I am left trudging through fear one heavy step at a time.
That place makes running feel like a memory.
Every step dragged at me like the ground wanted to keep me.
Please do not leave me somewhere escape itself feels tired.
The Soul Sand Valley made every sound feel hollow and every movement feel too slow.
I kept looking over my shoulder, knowing I could not get away quickly if I had to.
I was alone on soul sand, moving like a nightmare while the valley listened.
Don't leave me in the Warped Forest. Nothing there looks like it belongs anywhere safe.
The Warped Forest is too <wavy>strange</wavy> to be deserted in with a steady mind.
I waited in the Warped Forest trying not to stare too long at anything around me.
If you disappear in a Warped Forest, I am left alone in the sort of place that should stay imagined.
The colors were wrong, the silence was wrong, and I was very aware that I was alone.
I kept feeling like the forest had turned slightly while I was not looking.
Please do not leave me somewhere reality already feels loose.
The Warped Forest made every direction look familiar and impossible at the same time.
I could not tell if it was quiet because nothing was there or because everything was waiting.
Being left there felt like standing inside a bad dream that had learned my name.
